title: The Locked Room in the Sky: Shinichi Kudo's First Case
notes: Recurring detective-cast (Shinichi Kudo/Conan, Kogoro, Ran, Inspector Megure, Officer Takagi) omitted by convention, consistent with the ep11 prototype -- this holds even though the episode is framed as a flashback narrating Shinichi's literal first case. No `event` node type: actions are direct typed edges. This case contains a genuine evidence-based red herring distinct from a motive red herring: Edward Crowe is caught searching the already-dead victim's pockets for negatives and briefly looks like the killer (his cologne explains the victim's oddly wet trouser pocket), but is cleared once the blood-spatter/body-position evidence shows the body was moved after death by someone who hadn't seen how it was originally positioned -- kept as a circumstantial/opportunity red herring rather than a motive one, since the transcript gives him a business motive to buy the negatives but never a motive to kill. Two visually near-identical photo-negative objects appear and are kept as separate nodes per the schema's 'one node per physical instance' rule: the scandal negatives of Senator Dickson that drive the surface plot, and the separate incriminating arson photos that are the real motive evidence. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Wound-pattern clue: a peculiar scratch mark beside the fatal neck wound is consistent with the far (unsharpened) end of a thin wire scraping the skin during the stab -- a weapon shape not found on anyone in two full body/luggage searches except concealed in a bra underwire.

Testimony-consistency clue: cross-checking all four toilet-trip witnesses against each other, every account holds together except Amano's claim to have stayed asleep in her seat the whole time -- contradicted by Ukai's account of seeing her wandering the cabin.

Negative-fragment clue: a torn piece of film negative was found stuck to the seat beside Saginuma's, the seat with no assigned occupant on the manifest -- physical proof someone sat there who was carrying negative fragments, tying the disguise scheme directly to whoever was cutting up film that day.

Blood-position clue: blood was found on the restroom wall where the body was found leaning, but none on the body itself -- proving the body had been moved and repositioned after death by someone who found it, searched it (explaining the wet-yet-dry-handed pocket), and left without reporting it.

Arm-hesitation clue: reaching for luggage overhead, Amano's right arm stopped mid-motion and she switched to her left -- a tiny, otherwise meaningless tell consistent with a sharp object concealed against her right side pricking her.
